([[Albany, New York]]) | college = [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] (2020–2023) | draftyear = 2023 | draftround = 2 | draftpick = 36 | draftteam = [[Orlando Magic]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = →[[Wisconsin Herd]] | years3 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team3 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA Cup champions|NBA Cup champion]] ([[2024 NBA Cup|2024]]) * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023]]) }} '''Andre Terrell Jackson Jr.''' (born November 13, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]]. ==Early life and high school career== Jackson grew up in [[Amsterdam (city), New York|Amsterdam, New York]] and attended [[The Albany Academy]].{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-clb-uconn-men-andre-jackson-20191004-20191003-ezgzvt4vkfgwzl2fhfb36n7g5q-story.html|title=Meet Andre Jackson: Things to know about the newest UConn men's basketball player|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=October 3, 2019|last=Amore|first=Dom|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Jackson played on the United States select team in the 2018 [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1808115/2020/05/12/hes-like-a-leopard-coaches-rave-about-what-andre-jackson-brings-to-uconn/|title=‘He’s like a leopard’: Coaches rave about what Andre Jackson brings to UConn|first=Charlotte|last=Carroll|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=May 12, 2020|access-date=March 7, 2023}} He averaged 18.8 points, 10.1 rebounds, 5.1 assists, and three steals per game during his senior season and was named the New York Sports Writers Association Class A Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://dailygazette.com/2020/04/23/albany-academy-basketball-s-jackson-is-nysswa-class-a-player-of-year/|title=Albany Academy basketball's Jackson is NYSSWA Class A Player of Year|work=[[The Daily Gazette]]|date=April 23, 2020|last=Kelly|first=Michael|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Jackson committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] over offers from [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/27753291/espn-100-andre-jackson-commits-uconn-huskies|title=ESPN 100 Andre Jackson commits to UConn|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=October 2, 2019|access-date=March 7, 2023}} ==College career== Jackson played in 16 games during his freshman season at UConn and averaged 2.7 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 1.6 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-amore-column-uconn-men-liu-20211114-20211118-2lohwrvd65gezbkygcdhxg3cnu-story.html|title=Dom Amore: This is the Andre Jackson UConn men have been waiting for|first=Dom|last=Amore|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=November 18, 2021|access-date=March 7, 2023}} He missed seven games due to a broken left wrist.{{cite web|url=https://www.nhregister.com/uconn/article/UConn-freshman-Andre-Jackson-sidelined-15825266.php|title=UConn freshman Andre Jackson's broken wrist injury adds to tough week for Huskies|work=[[New Haven Register]]|date=December 23, 2020|last=Borges|first=David|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Jackson started all but one of the Huskies' games as a sophomore and averaged 6.8 points and 6.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-uconn-men-andre-jackson-ready-to-lead-20220515-20220515-vjk3gyrq4zdzbnvtzhqm3t7uuu-story.html|title=After roster shakeup, UConn guard Andre Jackson is ready to take charge|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=May 15, 2022|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Jackson was named a team captain entering his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-amore-column-uconn-men-big-east-andre-jackson-team-captain-20221020-20221019-gbhb7vyiifbf3lbg7zk2hkgtae-story.html|title=Dom Amore: How Andre Jackson Jr. became the captain Dan Hurley never knew he needed for UConn men's basketball|first=Dom|last=Amore|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=October 19, 2022|access-date=March 7, 2023}} He missed the first three games of the season after fracturing the pinky finger on his right hand during preseason practices.{{cite web|url=https://sny.tv/articles/uconn-andre-jackson-jr-fractured-pinky-underwent-successful-surgery|title=UConn's Andre Jackson Jr. suffered fractured pinky, underwent successful surgery|first=Robert|last=Sanchez|website=[[SNY.tv]]|date=October 12, 2022|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Jackson started the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|2023 national championship game]] and scored three points with six assists, three rebounds, and two steals as the Huskies won 76–59.{{cite web|url=https://dailygazette.com/2023/04/04/amsterdams-jackson-played-big-role-in-uconns-national-championship-win/|title=Amsterdam's Jackson played big role in UConn's national championship win|work=[[The Daily Gazette]]|date=April 4, 2023|access-date=April 10, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2023–2026)=== Jackson was selected with the 36th overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]], and was traded on draft night to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2023 |title=The @OrlandoMagic have acquired a future second round draft pick (2030) and cash considerations from Milwaukee in exchange for the draft rights to Andre Jackson Jr. (36th overall pick in 2023). |url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1672102346451558401 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230623120010/https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1672102346451558401 |archive-date=June 23, 2023 |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=[[Twitter]] |language=en}} On January 14, 2024, Jackson recorded his first career [[double-double]], with 10 points and 10 rebounds, during a 129–118 win over the [[2023–24 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web | last=Nehm | first=Eric | title=Andre Jackson Jr.'s 'big-time plays' help Bucks secure win over Warriors | website=The Athletic | date=2024-01-14 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5201280/2024/01/14/andre-jackson-jr-bucks-warriors/ | access-date=2025-12-06}} He made 57 appearances for Milwaukee during his rookie campaign, recording averages of 2.2 points and 2.0 rebounds.{{Cite web|title=Andre Jackson Jr. 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432190/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=September 5, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Jackson played in 67 games (including 43 starts) for the Bucks during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], logging averages of 3.4 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 1.2 assists.{{Cite web|title=Andre Jackson Jr. 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432190/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=September 5, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He made 48 appearances (including one starts) for Milwaukee in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 2.4 points and 1.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Andre Jackson Jr. 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432190/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=September 5, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Toronto Raptors (2026–present)=== On August 5, 2026, Jackson signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] on an [[Exhibit 10]] contract to compete for a roster spot.{{Cite web |date=August 5, 2026 |title=Raptors sign wing Andre Jackson Jr. |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-sign-wing-andre-jackson-jr/ |access-date=August 5, 2026|website=Sportsnet.ca |language=en}}{{Cite web |date= |title=Raptors
